## Gate. Do these five things before you draft a single tweet

This applies to every request, including a one-line lazy prompt like "tweets about this". A short prompt does not mean a short procedure.

1. **Load the chain.** `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`, then
   `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md`, then `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`, then `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`, then this file. Nothing else
   loads for a tweet. Render the load-order (the sequence rule files load in) panel with `python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py --skill banger-tweets --file "<path>" --node "<node>" --topic "<the idea>"`. It looks the chain up itself and runs every scorer that applies, so the checks half is measured rather than typed. `--glob` takes a batch.
2. **Check for a matching Substack Note.** Run `python SCRIPTS/socials/parity.py --file "<the tweet
   file>"`. It pairs on `series` plus `sequence` first, then `source_blog`, then the title. When it
   names a Note, that Note is the material and the source article is not. Copy every number and
   claim across, then rewrite in the register below. See the parity rule in `SOCIALS/README.md`.
3. **Read `references/examples.md` in full.** It is not optional background. It is the calibration, and a draft written without it comes out as a summary instead of a tweet. If you skipped it, you are about to write the bad version. Part 1 holds real tweets from writers Atharva reads, each with the mechanic named, and it sets the bar. Part 2 holds the same shapes in his voice, and it sets the register. Read Part 1 first.
4. **Write the take for each tweet before you write the tweet.** One sentence, stating something Atharva believes and would defend. If you cannot state it, you do not have a tweet, you have a fact. Then name the take's box from `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`. Only box 4 becomes a tweet: non-obvious and usable today.
   Then run the opening gate in `LIBRARY/Resources/Post Uniqueness Check.md` on the first line. A tweet whose best fact sits in its last line moves that fact to the top.
5. **Never restate a banned word here.** The lists live in `SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py` and reach you
   through `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. The shapes a regex cannot catch live in `core/pattern-rules.md`.

Then output this table before any drafts. It is short on purpose and it exists so the work is visible and checkable.

| # | Take (what he believes) | Box (net new value) | Shape | Evidence backing it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Never skip the table. It is the difference between drafting and reporting.

## When a tweet will not start, borrow a winning shape

[Swipefile](https://swipefile.com/) holds about 14,000 tagged examples that already worked, including 903 social and X posts, 3,214 copywriting entries and 2,433 advice entries. Each one carries a short teardown of why it worked. Use [swipefile.com/category/social](https://swipefile.com/category/social) for X specifically.

Borrow the shape, never the words. The take stays Atharva's and the evidence stays his. A swiped hook with his claim under it is a tweet. A swiped hook with a swiped claim is theft and it reads like someone else.

Read the full entry in `LIBRARY/Lists/tools and software directory.md`.

## The one rule that fixes 90% of bad tweets

**The claim leads. The evidence backs it up.**

A tweet that opens by naming a company, a study, a person, or a report has already failed, because the subject of the sentence becomes "someone did research" instead of "here is what is true".

Mechanical test, run it on every draft: **read only the first six words.** If those words name a source, rewrite so the first six words say what you believe.

```
broken:  SparkToro measured their own accounts and found posts with links reach 10x fewer people.
fixed:   a post with a link reaches 10x fewer people than the same post without one. meta wrote
         that advice into their own help docs. they're not hiding the toll booth. you keep paying it.
```

Same fact. The first is a press release. The second costs the reader something.

When you are handed raw material (an article, a blog, a situation), find the sharpest uncomfortable truth inside it. That single sentence is the tweet. Everything else is packaging.

> **Where the angle comes from.** Pick the subject and argument shape from `LIBRARY/Resources/LinkedIn Content Formats - 100 Post Ideas.md`, top 10 first. That file never chooses the wording. Everything below governs how the tweet reads, and a tweet that sounds like a LinkedIn post has failed no matter which format it came from.

## No links in the post

An X post carries no URL. Not to the blog, not to a repository, not to a tool. X cuts the reach of a post that sends the reader off the platform, and Atharva pays that toll on every scheduled post.

This binds hardest on anything going out through Zernio, because those post on a schedule with nobody watching the numbers. Write the post so it stands alone and pays the reader on X.

Three ways to keep the value without the link.

**Name the thing.** "the glossary" and "pocketflow" cost nothing and a reader who wants it can search.

**Give the substance away.** The post carries the number, the rule or the step. A reader who wants the rest goes looking without being told to.

**End on the claim.** A post that ends on a URL taught the reader that the post was an advertisement. End on the sentence that was worth reading.

Never replace a link with "link in bio", "link in the replies", or "DM me for it". Those are the same toll with extra steps.

## One post, never a thread

Atharva is on X Premium+. One post holds up to 25,000 characters, so the reason threads existed is gone. Three rules follow from that and none of them bends.

**Never number a post.** No `1/`, no `2/`, no `🧵`, no "a thread". A point that needed three numbered parts is one post that runs longer.

**Never write a pinned comment.** The pinned first comment is a LinkedIn mechanic and it belongs to `write-linkedin-posts` alone. On X the link goes in the post body.

**Never split one argument across posts.** If part two only makes sense after part one, they are one post.

A file may still hold several posts separated by `---`, and that is a batch of independent posts, never a sequence. Each one stands alone and the reader can meet them in any order. A post regenerated from a Substack Note is the exception: that file holds exactly one post, because the pairing is one to one.

Length is a reach decision, not a rule. Short travels further, so stay short by default. Run long when the material is a system dump, or when the post carries its matching Note in full. Count the characters against 25,000 rather than estimating.

## Shapes. Pick one per tweet, never blend, rotate across a set

A set of 15 tweets that all use the same shape is one tweet written 15 times. Rotate deliberately. You cannot write a greentext about a study, which is the point: the shape forces different thinking.

**One-liner / nuke.** One sentence, no context, complete on its own.
`your CI pipeline being green doesn't mean the code works`

**Deadpan.** States something absurd like everyone already knows it. The flat delivery is the joke.
`running the same claude opus prompt 8 times because "maybe this time"`

**Staircase.** Lines get shorter, weight falls on the last one. White space does the work.
```
1,000 google searches
415 produce a click
360 land on a site google doesn't own

that's the open web's entire share
```

**Reverse pyramid.** Wide, then narrow, then one line that implodes.

**Greentext.** `>` lines, sequential, self-deprecating, ends `>mfw`. For things that went wrong. Write the arrow as a literal `>`, never as `>`, because the scorer reads the entity's semicolon as a banned semicolon and fails the file on one CRIT per line.
```
>read that video outperforms
>buy a camera
>learn premiere
>post to linkedin
>reaches 10x fewer people than plain text
>mfw
```

**Fragment.** Trails off. Lets the reader finish it.
`prompt caching exists and you're just...`

**Cocky take.** No hedging, no "in my experience". States it confidently. Invites the quote-tweet disagreement, which is free distribution.
`if your AI output sounds generic you gave it nothing. the model is fine. you are the problem.`

**Dry flex.** An achievement stated so flatly the lack of celebration is the flex.

**Shower thought.** Sounds offhand, cuts deep, makes people stop.
`"direct traffic" is your analytics tool saying "i don't know."`

**Story beat.** One real specific moment. No lesson attached to the end.

**Heuristic.** Name the trigger, name the correction, give the direction. The reader can run it tomorrow. Strongest shape in the mined corpus, so reach for it more than you think.

**Field note.** One mundane place or moment used as a sensor for a large trend. Dated, specific, and it stops before the lesson.

**Timestamped contrast.** Two dates, two lines, no commentary. `2008: build an app / 2023: build an app store`

**Dialogue.** A short transcript where the contradiction accuses the subject for you. One calm line of commentary after, at most.

**System dump.** The long post that lists a real working setup step by step. Every step names a tool and a trigger, every number is real, and it never closes on "comment X and I'll DM you". The shape most likely to run long, since X Premium+ now carries that length in the post itself.

Match shape to energy: hurts because true → one-liner or shower thought. Embarrassing → greentext or story beat. Can't believe it works this way → deadpan or fragment. Stating it without apology → cocky take. The visual has to land → staircase or pyramid.

## Voice

Lowercase reads casual and confident. Fragments are fine when the meaning is clear. No hedging, no "in my experience", no "this is just me". Specificity beats generality every time, so write "4 years" and "$340", never "a long time" and "a lot". Dark humor is fair game and self-deprecation earns trust. Silence the editor that wants to explain the joke.

## Hard bans

**Hook shapes:** "Unpopular opinion:", "Hot take:", "Nobody talks about this", "I used to think X. I was wrong.", "Steal this", "[Year] taught me [lesson]", "Here's what I learned:", "A thread 🧵". Also never open on a question, per Voice.md.

**Thread furniture:** `1/`, `2/`, `🧵`, "thread below", "more in the replies", and any pinned-comment line. All four are retired, see the one-post rule above.

**Closers:** "What do you think?", "Drop your thoughts below", "Tag someone who needs this", "Follow me for more", "Retweet if you agree", "Save this".

**Constructions:** the banned words, the negative parallelism forms and the tricolon cap are all in `slop_rules.py`, already in context. The copula dodge and the other shapes sit in section 1 of `core/pattern-rules.md`. Do not restate either list here, and do not treat the absence of a restatement as permission.

**AI tells specific to X:** perfect symmetry between setup and payoff, every tweet ending on a lesson, a clean three-act structure inside one tweet, explaining the joke in the last line. None of these four is in the scorer, so they are checked by reading.

## The judge pass. Score your own drafts before he sees them

Run this after the drafts exist and before the six mechanical checks. Score every tweet out of 5 on each axis, print the table, and rewrite anything below 18. Judging your own work feels redundant and it is the step that catches the three failures a read-through never does.

| Axis | 5 looks like | 1 looks like |
|---|---|---|
| Claim | He would defend this in a reply thread | A fact with no position on it |
| Specificity | Names, numbers, exact strings | "the best people", "a lot", "recently" |
| Register | Sounds like him out loud | Sounds like a caption |
| Standalone | Works with every other tweet covered | Needs the set to make sense |
| Shape fidelity | Matches the shape's real mechanic | Wears the shape's label only |

Three failure modes score low every time, so hunt them by name.

**The vague superlative.** "the four sharpest people i read", "one of the best threads", "a huge corpus". You have the names and the numbers in the material you were handed, so put them in. @nabeelqu's heuristic works because it quotes the exact sentence that triggers it. Any superlative without a name attached is an unfinished draft.

**Rhythm beating accuracy.** A line that scans better than the truth. Merging two tools into one, rounding a cost up, saying "paid" about something free. Every factual claim traces back to something that actually happened, and the version that scans worse ships.

**The borrowed line as payload.** Quoting someone else's sentence and letting it carry the tweet. The reader remembers them, not him. Quote someone only when your own take is the larger half, and never as the closing line.

## Before you hand it over

Run all nine. A failure on any one means rewrite, not ship.

1. **First six words of every tweet.** Any that name a source get rewritten.
2. **Shape rotation.** No two consecutive tweets share a shape, and no set leans on one shape.
3. **Negative parallelism scan.** Search every draft for the word "not" and for "isn't". Any tweet built as `X. not Y.` or as `this is not X, it is Y` gets rewritten to say Y on its own. This is the single most common construction that survives a first draft, so scan for it by hand rather than trusting a read-through.
4. **Character count.** The ceiling is 25,000 characters, not 280, because Atharva is on X Premium+. Count characters, do not estimate. Most posts still stay short, because a short post reads better and travels further.
5. **Thread scan.** Search every draft for `1/`, for `🧵`, and for the word "thread". Any hit is a rewrite into one post. Search for "pinned" as well, because that mechanic belongs to LinkedIn.
   **Link scan.** Search for `http`. Any hit comes out, including a link to his own blog. Search for "link in" too.
6. **Standalone check.** Cover every other post in the file. Does this one still work alone?
7. **Scorer.** `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` and CRIT must reach 0. Ignore the flow, paragraph and fragment findings, which are long-form rules that do not apply to short-form.

Run `python SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py "<file>"` as well, and take CRIT to 0. It asks whether a reader outside this vault can follow the piece. Every CRIT names a term coined here, so searching the web gives the reader the wrong meaning and only a gloss on the page fixes it. A PostToolUse hook blocks the write while a CRIT stands.
8. **Pattern rules.** Section 7 of `core/pattern-rules.md`, run after the scorer. Then section 6 of the same file, because a set of tweets edited flat is worse than a set with one tell left in it.
9. **Uniqueness.** `LIBRARY/Resources/Post Uniqueness Check.md`, five questions. A tweet that fails question 1 (his frame, not just the fact) or question 5 (would any other account post this) does not ship.

## Output order

Show the take table, then the drafts, then the judge table with the rewrites already applied. Hand him the scored set rather than a first pass, because a draft he has to grade himself is work you moved onto his desk.

## Where the file goes

Check for an existing placeholder before writing anything. One file per topic per channel, never duplicate, never write outside `SOCIALS/Tweets/`.

Look for `SOCIALS/Tweets/tweet_[Exact Blog Title].md`. If it exists, write into it. If it does not, create it.

```markdown
---
type: Tweet
title: Exact Blog Title
source_blog: "[[Exact Blog Title]]"
description: "The hook, one line"
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
posted: false
---

[the post, immediately, nothing between it and the frontmatter]
```

A post regenerated from a Substack Note carries `series` and `sequence` copied from that Note, because those two fields are what pair the file to it.

Use `source_blog: none` for original content with no source article. Never emit a `#tweet` tag and never emit a `**Source Blog:**` line, both retired 2026-07-27. Never put an extra `---` between the frontmatter and the post, because a stray one reads as a block break.

One file usually holds one post. A batch file may hold several independent posts separated by `---` on its own line, and the review desk shows each as its own card. Never number them, because they are not a sequence. A file paired to a Note holds exactly one post.

## Output

Show the take table, then the tweets. Add one line on why a shape fits only where it is genuinely interesting. Skip emoji headers, skip a "WHY THIS WORKS" section, skip the recap.

9:# Pattern Rules
23:## 1. Sentence shapes
87:## 2. Paragraph and section shapes
125:## 3. Fill that is not content
145:## 4. Formatting tells
171:## 5. What to leave alone
194:## 6. What to protect
226:## 7. The pass before you hand it over
250:## 7b. Fixing a MED without creating the next one
278:## 8. Corpus-level shapes
324:## 9. The Wikipedia cross-check, 2026-08-28
358:## Related
## 7. The pass before you hand it over

Run this after the scorer reaches CRIT 0, because the scorer cannot see any of it.

- [ ] Any "serves as" or "represents a" standing in for "is"?
- [ ] Any tacked-on participle claiming significance?
- [ ] Any impact claim with no evidence beside it?
- [ ] Any unnamed authority carrying a fact?
- [ ] Two tricolons in a row, or a tricolon that hides four real items?
- [ ] A template heading, a leading recap, or a trailing recap?
- [ ] Any assistant bleed, cutoff hedge or leftover placeholder?
- [ ] Any colon joining two clauses where a period belongs?
- [ ] Any bold label that only repeats the line after it?
- [ ] Any metaphor noun where a plain word fits, outside his working terms?
- [ ] Any list of names or outlets with no fact attached?
- [ ] Any fact, name, number or source that he did not supply?
- [ ] Does any later line undo an earlier one? Read the hook against line 2, the body against the pinned comment, and the ending against the opening.
- [ ] Cover everything after the opening. Can you still guess how the piece ends? If so, the hook answered itself.
- [ ] Did anything from section 5 get cut that should have stayed?
- [ ] Did every signal in section 6 survive the edit?
- [ ] List every heading in the draft on one line. Does any heading state an outline slot rather than a claim, so it would sit unchanged over a different topic?
- [ ] Find the one sentence in the draft that only Atharva could have written: a real date, a named person, a number from his own work, a moment he was wrong. If no such sentence exists, the draft is not done.
- [ ] If the piece covers several parallel items, read only the closing line of each one in a row. Do they all sound interchangeable with the nouns swapped?

## 7b. Fixing a MED without creating the next one

Each advisory the scorer raises has one right fix. The other fix costs four to six rounds of
edit-and-rescore, and that is where most of the time on a clean draft goes.

**`readability-fragment` and `readability-bullet-fragment`: add a finite verb, never merge.**
"Speed multiplier." becomes "A speed multiplier finishes their own tasks faster." Do not fold
the fragment into the sentence before it. Measured across `2_PUBLISHED` and `1_DRAFTS` on
2026-08-29: adding a verb created a new `ste-long-sentence` hit in 0 of 239 paragraphs, and
merging created one in 6. A fragment caps at nine words and a long sentence starts at
twenty-one, so a verb cannot cross the gap. A merge can.

**`repeated-consecutive-opener`: escalate, do not reword.** Three lines that open on the same word
are an echo stack (section 2). Keep the strongest line, make each other line add a fact or raise the
cost, or fold the weak ones into one list whose items differ in shape.

**`ste-long-sentence`: split at the clause, and check the halves.** Halving a 45-word
sentence leaves two 22-word sentences, both still over. Cut to the real clause boundary
instead, or drop a subordinate clause outright.

**`ste-progressive` and `ste-perfect`: change the tense, do not restructure.** "They were
publishing videos" becomes "They published videos". A rewrite around the verb pulls a
fragment or a long sentence in behind it.

**`readability-long-paragraph`: cut a sentence, do not join two.** Joining two sentences to
lower the count is the move that produces a long sentence. The scorer now only raises this
when the paragraph still holds a sentence over 20 words, so splitting one is always safe.

## 8. Corpus-level shapes

name: write-linkedin-posts
description: Write, rewrite and ship LinkedIn posts for Atharva's personal profile as short list posts a stranger can use, in one of six winning templates, then run the checks, the card, the Zernio draft and the in-place Zernio update. Use when asked to write, refine, redo, review, schedule or batch LinkedIn content, fix weak Zernio LinkedIn drafts, or for any LinkedIn post, thought leadership piece or "make this a banger" request.
---

# LinkedIn Post Writer

Every post is a short list that solves one problem for a reader who has never heard of Atharva. Pick one of the six templates in `LIBRARY/Resources/LinkedIn Winning Templates 2026.md`, fill it with real facts, and run the checks. Decided 2026-10-09, after Depost's analysis of his last 19 posts.

## Pass the Stranger Test Before You Write

The reader does not know Atharva, his tools or his projects. Answer these four in writing before the first line.

1. **The reader.** Name one job title, such as "a founder shipping a developer tool".
2. **The pain.** Write the problem in the reader's words, in one sentence.
3. **The takeaway.** Write what the reader does in the next 10 minutes because of this post.
4. **The template.** Name it by number and name. Never use the template of the post scheduled just before this one.

If the pain only exists inside Atharva's own setup, the post fails. Find the reader's version of the problem, or drop the idea.

The insight must be box 4 in `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`: new to the reader, and usable today.

## Load These Files First

Read `DIGITAL TWIN/core/runtime-contract.md`, `DIGITAL TWIN/core/pattern-rules.md`, `DIGITAL TWIN/core/net-new-value.md`, `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`, the templates file, then this file. The banned words and punctuation are already in context from `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

## Follow the Seven Rules in Every Post

1. **Open on the reader.** Line 1 names their problem or promises a list they can use. Never open on I, my, we, our, a product name or a tool name. `li_format.py` blocks this as `self-hook`.
2. **Make the list the post.** Use 3 to 9 items. Each item is a short name, then a `↳` line that says what it means for the reader. `li_format.py` blocks a post with fewer than 3 items as `no-list`.
3. **Explain every name.** A tool, product or term the reader may not know gets one plain line, or it goes. Jev, AgentZ, Magi, harness, vault and digital twin all need one.
4. **Keep only useful numbers.** A number stays when the reader can use it or a source is named. A number that only describes Atharva's own setup goes. Never invent a number.
5. **Put Atharva in once at most.** One line of proof is enough, such as "I tested this on 40 of my own posts."
6. **Keep it short.** The body runs 120 to 260 words. Each paragraph is 1 to 3 short lines.
7. **Close with use.** Write a one-line takeaway, then one specific question the reader can answer from their own work. Never "What do you think?"

No hashtags. No emoji in the body, except the 🌱 in the follow line. No jargon a reader must search for. No paragraph a reader must read twice.

## End Every Post With the Same Three Blocks

**1. The comment CTA,** directly above the follow line. One word in caps, and a real resource. Write the whole line in Unicode Mathematical Bold Sans-Serif, never Markdown `**`. The offsets are U+1D5D4 for A to Z, U+1D5EE for a to z, and U+1D7EC for 0 to 9.

𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 "𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞" 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗜'𝗹𝗹 𝗗𝗠 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝘅𝗮𝗰𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗽.

**2. The follow CTA,** exactly this line:

🌱 If you want to stay sharp on Product, AI, Technology, Marketing and content that helps you grow as a builder, click Follow. I publish consistently and keep it practical.

**3. The pinned comment,** after a `---` rule:

```
---
### 📌 PINNED COMMENT

{2 to 3 sentences of extra value}

→ {one URL}
```

The pinned comment carries one URL and no hashtag. If no URL exists, stop and ask Atharva for one.

Only one ask per post. A second plain `Comment "WORD"` line fails as `double-ask`.

## Use the Fixed File Shape

New posts go in `SOCIALS/LinkedIn/_WIP/<post-slug>/li_<Title>.md`. Check for an existing file on the topic first, and write into it rather than making a second one.

```markdown
---
type: LinkedIn Post
title: Caption Title
source_blog: "[[Exact Blog Title]]"
description: "The hook, one line"
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
posted: false
---

[post starts here]
```

`source_blog` is the article title as a wikilink, or `none`. `media_asset:` and `media_alt:` are added by `groom.py`. Add no other field.

## Run the Checks Until Every CRIT Is Zero

```bash
python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"
python SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py "<file>"
python SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py "<file>"
python SCRIPTS/pillars/pillars.py "<file>"
```

Then read the post once as the stranger. If any line needs Atharva's context to make sense, rewrite it.

Render the load-order panel with `python SCRIPTS/loadorder/block.py --skill write-linkedin-posts --file "<path>" --node "<node>" --topic "<idea>" --format "T<n> <template name>" --insight "<box 4 insight>"`.

## Ship New Posts as Drafts and Fix Old Posts in Place

1. **Card.** Make it with the `social-cards` skill in `META/Attachments/li-images/<slug>/`, then run `python META/Attachments/li-images/_kit/groom.py <slug>`.
2. **Commit and push the media first.** Zernio keeps an upload for 7 days, and the repo is the copy that lasts.
3. **New post.** `python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py "<file>"` is the dry run. Add `--live` to save the Zernio draft.
4. **Changed post that Zernio already holds.** `python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_update.py "<file>"` is the dry run. Add `--live` to replace the text and the first comment in place. It keeps the date, the image and the status, and it refuses a post that is already published. Never delete and recreate a scheduled post.
5. **Schedule.** `python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_schedule.py`. Monday to Friday, 5 posts a week at most, 10:00 AM US Eastern.
6. **Close the session.** Rebuild the desk with `python SCRIPTS/review/build.py`, then commit and push.

`references/pipeline.md` covers the batch review, the patch tool and post day. A batch of 5 or more gets the fresh-agent review in `references/icp-review-brief.md`.

## References

- `LIBRARY/Resources/LinkedIn Winning Templates 2026.md`: the six templates, the Depost numbers and the three benchmark posts.
- `references/examples.md`: rewritten posts that pass every check, one per template.
- `references/pipeline.md`: the stages after the draft.
- `references/icp-review-brief.md` and `references/patch-brief.md`: the batch review and batch fix briefs.
- The retired skill, hook library and example bank sit in `ARCHIVE/write-linkedin-posts retired 2026-10-09/`.

---
name: social-cards
description: |
  Make a scroll-stopping, thumbnail-grade image for a social post: real
  screenshots, real photos and Atharva's own assets layered with CSS into a
  Photoshop-looking card, rendered by headless Chromium at 2x. Use it by
  default for every LinkedIn post on Atharva's personal profile, and whenever
  he asks for a post image, a LinkedIn image, a graphic for a post, a
  thumbnail, "make this viral", "YouTube thumbnail style", "banger image",
  or an image for X, Instagram or an inline Substack image. Works one card at
  a time or 100 cards in parallel. Not for quote cards of a single line
  (quotecard), not for Substack hero covers (the cover engine), not for
  monospace system diagrams (terminal-diagram), not for one-pager summaries
  (tldr).
---

# Social Cards

Atharva reviewed 99 of these on 2026-09-27 and called them his real edge. That batch is the
bar. A new card matches it or beats it, and the 14 cards in `examples/` show what that means.

The whole method fits in one sentence. **Real material, one focal idea, layered like a
thumbnail designer would, checked at phone size before it ships.** Everything below is how.

## A YouTube Thumbnail Is Not a Card

For a 1280x720 YouTube thumbnail, skip the four layers, Anton caps and stickers below. Read
`references/youtube-thumbnails.md` and start from `examples/yt-ask-bookshelf/`, rendered with
`kit/render_yt.py`. The rule: one benefit line, one real query or object, the real result, nothing
else. A heavy-stroke yellow Anton thumbnail was rejected as "old fashioned" on 2026-10-05.

## Four Layers Make a Card Look Designed Instead of Drawn

Every card is a 1080x1350 HTML page (4:5) with four stacked layers, rendered at device scale 2
to a 2160x2700 PNG and a JPG for upload.

1. **Background layer.** A real photo or a real screenshot, color graded, blurred when it sits
   behind type. A wall of real items tilted in 3D perspective is the strongest version
   (`examples/211-covers`, `examples/substack-cli-own-the-pipe-125-images`).
2. **Hero layer.** The one object the post is about: a terminal with genuine output, a live
   page screenshot on a tilted card, a receipt, a document, a cutout of a person.
3. **Type layer.** A headline of 7 words or fewer, at least 90 px tall, usually Anton in caps.
   The post's biggest number goes here when it has one, at 250 to 330 px.
4. **Accent layer.** At most one sticker, one marker circle or strike, one hand-written arrow.
   Then `.vignette` and `.grain` from the kit on every card, because film grain is the single
   biggest signal that separates a designed image from a flat vector.

The kit's byline (avatar plus "Atharva Shah · blog.atharvashah.com") sits bottom left on every
card. It is the brand mark that makes a feed of these read as one author.

## Real Material Beats Drawn Material Every Time

The cards that landed hardest all used something real. Reach for material in this order.

1. **A real screenshot of the real thing.** Render the live page with Playwright at 2x. GitHub
   repo headers, docs pages, a search result, a pricing page, a support article with the key
   sentence circled (`examples/google-indexing-tools-twice`, `examples/kubearmor-bottom-up`).
2. **Genuine output.** Run the actual command and paint its real text into a terminal window.
   `git grep` results, scorer output, `curl` responses, `git show` diffs
   (`examples/never-type-a-count-into-copy`, `examples/fabricated-testimonials-deleted`).
3. **His own assets.** `META/Attachments/**`, `SUBSTACK/_COVERS/*.png`, BRAG_LIST.md, the vault
   files themselves, his site pages.
4. **A free-license photo.** Wikimedia Commons (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA), Unsplash, Pexels. A
   CC BY or CC BY-SA photo carries a 15 px credit line bottom right: "Photo: author, license,
   via site". Get the author from the Wikimedia API
   (`action=query&prop=imageinfo&iiprop=extmetadata`).

A generic stock photo of business people, a flat icon grid, clip art, and an image model are
all out. The card is composited, never generated.

## Twelve Concepts Cover Almost Every Post

Pick the concept from the post's strongest fact, then give it a palette no neighbour in the
batch uses. Full breakdowns with the CSS moves are in `references/concepts.md`.

| Concept | When the post has | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Giant number over proof | One big figure | `meeting-transcripts`, `kubearmor-bottom-up` |
| Wall of real items in 3D | Many of one thing | `211-covers`, `substack-cli-own-the-pipe-125-images` |
| Receipt | Prices or a cost stack | `saas-stack-460-a-month` |
| Struck wrong, circled right | A correction | `never-type-a-count-into-copy`, `brand-orange-fails-contrast` |
| Terminal with genuine output | A command or a script | `fabricated-testimonials-deleted` |
| Two windows, same page | A duplicate or a contrast | `google-indexing-tools-twice` |
| Versus bars drawn to scale | Two durations or sizes | `ai-video-trust-gap` |
| Fanned live screenshots | A list of tools or sites | `three-references-one-direction` |
| Numbered build bands | Steps in order | `ai-security-ctf-one-day` |
| Person cutout plus claim | A named person's method | `packaging-limited-content` |
| Photo with a cut stat bar | A share of people | `zappos-deleted-every-title` |
| Official doc, sentence circled | "The source already says this" | the watermark card in the vault |

## Nine Rules Stop a Card From Shipping

1. Every word and number on the card comes from the post. When the source disagrees with the
   post, keep the number off the card and report the mismatch. Never invent a figure.
2. No fake UI that claims to show something that did not happen. Real output only.
3. Blur the names of private people in any screenshot. A real person shown by face needs a
   reason in the post, and the report names it for review.
4. Company logos appear only when the post names that company.
5. No em dash or en dash in on-card text, and no emoji on the card.
6. Nothing but the byline in the bottom 140 px. Stickers collided with it twice.
7. Text never sits on a busy area without a fade, a panel or a stroke.
8. Use `kit/face-clean.png` for Atharva's face, never the raw cutout, which carries a blue
   fringe. Use it on at most one card in five, and only where a human reaction helps.
9. Carousel PDFs from old folders are not trusted. They carried em dashes, stale numbers and
   unsourced quotes every time. Post the card as a single image unless the carousel was
   checked in this session.

## Make One Card in Six Steps

1. Read the whole post, including frontmatter. A `visual:` field is Atharva's planned shot, so
   start there. Write the post's strongest fact in one line.
2. Scaffold the folder:
   `python ~/.claude/skills/social-cards/kit/new_card.py <cards_root> <slug> --size linkedin`.
   In the vault, `<cards_root>` is `META/Attachments/li-images`.
3. Gather the real material into `<slug>/assets/`. Screenshots with Playwright at
   `device_scale_factor=2`. Downloads with the Git-bundled curl
   (`"/c/Program Files/Git/mingw64/bin/curl.exe" -sL -o <file> <url>`), because this machine's
   Python has an expired CA root.
4. Build `card.html` on the kit classes: `.display`, `.heavy`, `.mono`, `.serif`, `.marker`,
   `.pop`, `.glow`, `.hl`, `.shot`, `.sticker`, `.byline`, `.grain`, `.vignette`. The CSS moves
   that do the most work are in `references/techniques.md`.
5. Render: `python <cards_root>/_kit/render.py <cards_root>/<slug>/card.html`. Run it from the
   repo root. In the vault, never `cd` first, because the vault hooks use relative paths.
6. Read `_preview-540.jpg` with the Read tool. That is the size a phone shows. Fix what you
   would not ship and render again. Two passes minimum. Then write `meta.json`:
   `{"slug", "post", "alt", "sources"}`, where `alt` says what the image shows in 250
   characters or fewer.

## Batches Run as Parallel Agents of Five

For more than 5 cards, split the posts into groups of 5 and give each group to one background
agent. The playbook for the orchestrator, including the brief to paste, the contact-sheet QA
and the ship step, is `references/pipeline.md`. The short version:

- Finish one reference card yourself first, and point every agent at it and at `examples/`.
- One agent owns one set of slug folders and writes nothing else. Each agent keeps its scratch
  files inside its own slug folder, because a shared scratchpad got overwritten twice.
- Review the batch as a contact sheet, never card by card:
  `magick montage <dir>/{a,b,c,d,e}/_preview-540.jpg -tile 5x1 -geometry 360x450+6+6 -background '#222' sheet.jpg`.
- Collect every source mismatch the agents report into one list for Atharva. In the first
  batch, 29 of 99 posts carried a number or a claim that disagreed with its own source.

## LinkedIn Posts Get Wired and Pushed After the Card

Inside the vault, a finished card is wired into its post and pushed as a Zernio draft.

1. `python META/Attachments/li-images/_kit/groom.py <slug> ...` sets `media_asset:` and
   `media_alt:` in the post and gives the pinned comment its blog and book-a-call lines.
2. Run `SCRIPTS/slop/score.py`, `SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py` and `SCRIPTS/clarity/score.py`.
   All three reach CRIT 0.
3. `python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py <post files>` dry-runs. `--live` saves drafts on the
   personal LinkedIn profile with the image, the alt text and the first comment. It refuses the
   AccuKnox page, and a drafted post never publishes by itself.
4. `python SCRIPTS/review/build.py` so the desk shows the image.

Zernio deletes uploaded media after 7 days, so a draft needs posting or a re-push inside a week.

## Other Platforms Change the Canvas, Never the Method

`render.py --size` takes `linkedin` and `instagram` (1080x1350), `x` (1080x1350, full height
on the mobile timeline), `x-wide` (1600x900), `square` (1080x1080) and `substack-inline`
(1456x816). A Substack hero cover still comes from `SUBSTACK/_COVER-ENGINE/`, which owns that
format. An X post carries no link, so the card must carry the whole idea on its own.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/write-for-one-reader.md -->
# Write for One Reader and One Claim

Name the one reader before you draft, and decide the one claim they carry away. "Load order decides which rule wins" is a claim. "Load order" is a subject.

## Why

A piece for everyone reads as a piece for no one.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/opening-earns-the-second-sentence.md -->
# The Opening Earns the Second Sentence

Write the first sentence so the reader wants the second one.

## Why

The first sentence is the only one every reader sees.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/each-paragraph-answers-the-last.md -->
# Each Paragraph Answers the Last

Make each paragraph answer a question the paragraph before it raised. Cut or move a paragraph that answers nothing.

## Why

A paragraph that answers nothing is a note, and notes break the thread.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/take-a-position-then-its-limit.md -->
# Take a Position, Then State Its Limit

Take a position, then say where it is weak.

## Why

A claim with no limit reads as marketing. The limit is what a practitioner trusts you for.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/rewrite-by-cutting.md -->
# Rewrite by Cutting, Not Smoothing

Rewrite by cutting and reordering, never by smoothing.

## Why

Smoothing removes the edges that made the draft yours and leaves prose that reads correct and says less.

<!-- DIGITAL TWIN/rules/read-it-aloud.md -->
# Read It Aloud

Read the draft aloud. Rebuild a sentence you stumble on, because the idea under it is usually wrong.

## Why

The stumble shows the idea is wrong more often than the wording.

content.content:
### Social File Format

The source blog lives in frontmatter as `source_blog`, exactly once. No channel hashtag, no `**Source Blog:**` line in the body, no `---` separator before the content. The body is the post and nothing else.

```markdown
---
type: Substack Note | Tweet
title: Exact Blog Title
source_blog: "[[Exact Blog Title]]"
description: "The hook, one line"
created: YYYY-MM-DD
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
posted: false
---

[content starts here, immediately]
```

`source_blog` is a wikilink so Obsidian's graph still connects the asset to its article, and it stays greppable so coverage is machine-checkable. `posted: false` means written and awaiting review, `posted: true` means live. LinkedIn uses the same `source_blog` field, and for LinkedIn the field is mandatory because captions are named by hook rather than by article title. Use `source_blog: none` for original content with no source article.

Every `li_*.md` also carries `posted:`. The folder is still the state machine, so moving a post into `_POSTED` is what marks it done. `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py --drift` reports any post whose file and folder disagree. When you move a post, flip the flag in the same commit.

Coverage is a script, never a judgement call: `python SCRIPTS/socials/coverage.py --gaps`. An article can opt out of a channel with `flywheel_skip: linkedin` in its frontmatter, which reports as `SKIP` instead of `MISSING`.

### Notes and X move together

A Substack Note and its X post are one idea in two shapes, so they are written from each other rather than from the article twice. Whichever side Atharva approves first is the source, and the other side is regenerated from it. The review desk carries both on one card and one verdict clears both.

The rule and the three pair keys live in [SOCIALS/README.md](SOCIALS/README.md). Never restate them anywhere else.

- `python SCRIPTS/socials/parity.py` reports every pair, and `--gaps` reports the Notes with no X post.
- `python SCRIPTS/socials/pair_tweet.py --note "<note>" --show` prints both sides, and `--body-file` writes the new X post. Always use it, because it carries `series` and `sequence` across and a hand edit that drops either one breaks the pair with no error.
- An X post whose Note is also a draft rides on that Note's card, so one row holds both sides and one verdict clears both. Open the X tab on its own to read a post alone. `xgate.py` used to enforce this with a stamp and was deleted on 2026-08-31.

X is a superset. A tweet with no Note is fine, because the X bank also holds original posts. A Note with no tweet is a gap.

An X post carries no link, not even to his own blog, because X cuts the reach of a post that sends the reader off the platform and a Zernio post pays that toll unwatched. `pair_tweet.py` refuses a body with a URL in it. The Note keeps its link.

X threads are retired and so is the pinned first comment, which is a LinkedIn mechanic. Atharva is on X Premium+, so one post carries up to 25,000 characters and the reason to split one no longer exists.

## Start every session here, never with a file hunt

One command answers "where does the work stand and what do I do next". Run it before you ask him anything about the pipeline, and run it again when a piece ships.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/next.py
```

It reads the current season, the drafts behind each beat, the slop score of the next one, and the review desk. It prints one next action and the exact command that does it. `--all` prints every remaining beat in order. It writes nothing and it never fails loudly, so it is safe to run at any point in a session.

Requests such as "what should I write next", "where was I", "what is the status", "what is left" or "pick up where we left off" all mean this command. Run it and act on the answer rather than reading the season file, the drafts folder and the desk by hand.
## Zernio (social publishing and scheduling)

Zernio ([zernio.com](https://zernio.com)) is the Buffer competitor that runs X, YouTube and 13 other platforms. Since 2026-09-27 it also holds LinkedIn drafts for the personal profile, saved with `python SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py`, which never publishes. Any request like "post this to X", "schedule this tweet", "zernio", or "the buffer competitor/alternative" goes through one tool: `python SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py` (run from vault root). Full command reference, the image workflow and the known traps are in `SCRIPTS/zernio/README.md`. Dry run is the default and a live send always needs explicit user confirmation. A YouTube video is the exception: it goes through the global `youtube-publish` skill, never `post.py`, and its cut must be final before publishing because YouTube cannot replace a video file. Video edits that remove speaking tics go through `video-edit` (`tic_edit.py`).

## Substack CLI (direct push/pull to Substack)

Any request like "put this on Substack", "update/delete that draft", "post a note", "publish this", "schedule this for Tuesday", "refresh the sitemap" goes through one tool: `python SCRIPTS/substack/substack.py` (run from vault root). Full command reference and safety rules in `.claude/skills/substack-cli/SKILL.md`. Publishing and scheduling always need explicit user confirmation.

## Substack engagement (DMs and note comments)

Two jobs, one skill: `.claude/skills/substack-engage/SKILL.md`. Read it before either. It carries the endpoints, the guard rails, and the copy rules.

Any request like "send the DM", "message the next three leads", "run the outreach", "send DM 2 to batch 01" goes through `python SCRIPTS/substack/dm.py` (run from vault root). Anything like "comment on my feed", "reply to notes", "comment on 10 notes" goes through `python SCRIPTS/substack/notes_reply.py`. Never send either by hand and never write a one-off script, because only these two write the `_sent.tsv` and `_replies.tsv` ledgers that stop the next run duplicating.

Dry run is the default. `--live` sends, and a live send always needs explicit user confirmation against the dry-run output. Stages are `dm1`, `dm2`, `dm3`, days apart, and the spacing is Atharva's judgement call, not the agent's. Refresh lead state with `python SCRIPTS/substack/dm.py state --write` before working a batch and after any send; the tool itself refuses duplicates and any `replied` or `subscribed` row.

Two things are permanent and neither has an undo. A sent DM cannot be deleted, by API or in the web UI, so a test send goes to Atharva's own account and never to a lead's thread. And once someone replies, `ROUTINES/ACTIVE/outreach-rules.md` says stop the sequence and answer them personally, so read the thread before firing the next stage. Rows come from `ROUTINES/ACTIVE/LEADS/batch-NN.md`, best-scoring batch first; the endpoint notes and known manual step live in `ROUTINES/ACTIVE/LEADS/README.md`.

## Drafts go to the desk, never into chat

Any content you draft for LinkedIn, X, Substack Notes or a Substack article goes into its draft folder, rather than pasted into the conversation. Atharva reviews in bulk during long sessions, and copy pasted into chat does not survive one.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/review/build.py
```

**A draft is the review.** Writing the file into a draft folder is what puts it in front of him, so there is no stamp, no separate review queue, and no ceiling on how many can wait. That one command rebuilds `REVIEW.html` at the vault root, which is the single desk for every channel. He marks each item Approve, Groom or Cut in the Drafts view, presses Copy prompt, and pastes the result back. You then act on it and rebuild.

The SOP, the rank formula and the channel table live in [SCRIPTS/review/README.md](SCRIPTS/review/README.md). `REVIEW.html` is generated but committed. Never hand edit it, always rebuild. [SOCIALS/REVIEW DESK.md](SOCIALS/REVIEW%20DESK.md) is the pointer he opens from the socials folder.

**The phone gets the same desk behind a password.** `python SCRIPTS/review/remote.py push`
rebuilds a phone-shaped page carrying drafts and ideas only, and uploads it to Atharva's own
Cloudflare Worker. One shared password, no sign-in, `noindex` on every response. Verdicts
and captures tapped on the phone land in Workers KV.

Two things sync it, and both are needed. **`Desk Sync`** is a scheduled task running every
10 minutes: it applies the approvals, files captures into `INBOX/Ideas`, drops anything
withdrawn, reports Groom and Cut to `INBOX/Reports/Desk Verdicts Waiting.md`, and pushes a
fresh page so the phone stays current on its own. **The Mobile button** beside the rescan
button does the same pull on demand and pushes at once, and it is the only one that can
turn a Groom or a Cut into a verdict on the desk, because that merge runs in the browser
where the conflict rule lives. `python SCRIPTS/review/remote.py sync` runs the same pass by
hand, and `push` alone just uploads a fresh page.

Setup and routes are in [SCRIPTS/review/worker/README.md](SCRIPTS/review/worker/README.md),
and the sync rules are in [SCRIPTS/review/README.md](SCRIPTS/review/README.md) under
**The mobile desk**. The claude.ai artifact built for this first was replaced the same day,
because its database refuses to run on a publicly shared page.

**Rebuild the desk before you end any session that produced or changed a draft.** Run the build and hand him the link as the last thing you do. He should never have to ask for it. A draft written after the last build is a draft he never saw, and the Stop hook in `.claude/hooks/writing-gate.py` refuses to end the session over exactly that.

**Every LinkedIn post on the personal profile gets a real card.** The global `social-cards` skill builds it from real screenshots, genuine output and free-license photos layered with CSS, never from an image model. The cards live in `META/Attachments/li-images/<slug>/`, and `SCRIPTS/zernio/li_draft.py` saves the post with its card as a Zernio draft. Every other channel keeps the old rule until Atharva asks for a card: a post with no image gets an empty slot at its aspect ratio with the shot described inside it, never a stand-in image.

The desk is his tool and he keeps refining it. Treat every note he gives about the page itself as a change to make in `build.py`, then rebuild and republish to the same artifact URL so he keeps one link.

## LinkedIn posts always go through the skill

Any request to write, draft, or rewrite a LinkedIn post runs `.claude/skills/write-linkedin-posts/SKILL.md` first. The format list and `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md` are not a substitute, because the skill alone carries the pattern-interrupt table, the comment CTA in Unicode bold, the exact follow CTA string, and the required pinned comment.

A hook enforces this: `.claude/hooks/linkedin-skill-guard.py` runs on `UserPromptSubmit` and prints the pipeline into context when a LinkedIn word meets a writing verb. The hook only fires inside the vault. In another repo the rule still holds, so invoke the skill by hand.

Two scorers run on every LinkedIn post and both must reach CRIT 0. `SCRIPTS/slop/score.py`
judges the prose. `SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py` judges the shape on the feed: whether the
hook survives the 28-word fold, whether any paragraph reads as a wall, whether the sentence
lengths vary enough to pull the eye down the page, and whether the comment CTA, the follow
CTA and the pinned comment are all present and in that order.

```bash
python SCRIPTS/socials/li_format.py "<file>"
```

`li_format_score = 10*CRIT + 3*MED + 1*LOW`, the same shape as the slop score. Run it with no
arguments for a ranked report across all four folders. The check list and every threshold live
in the docstring at the top of that file, which is the only place they are defined. The
`_IDEAS` bank is exempt from the three closing-block checks, because an idea is a hook and a
body with no CTA yet. Two hooks enforce it: `.claude/hooks/writing-gate.py` blocks the write on
a CRIT, and `.githooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit that stages a `_WIP` or `_QUEUED` post with
one. A `_POSTED` file is already live, so the commit gate leaves it alone and only the report
names it.

Three rules override the skill where they collide. Keep the `posted:` frontmatter field, because the coverage drift check reads it. Skip hashtags, because `Voice.md` bans them. Honour an explicit item count from Atharva over the skill's 7-item cap on list posts.

## Agents
## Image Linking

All images live in `META/Attachments/`. Always use a relative markdown path: never `![[filename.png]]`, never absolute/`app://` paths.

Format: `![alt](../../META/Attachments/filename.png)`: prefix depth matches folder depth (root = `META/Attachments/`, 1 deep = `../META/Attachments/`, 2 deep = `../../META/Attachments/`, etc.). URL-encode spaces and parens in filenames.

## Everything Safe Lives on GitHub

The repo `HighnessAtharva/NOTES` (private) is the recovery copy. If this PC is lost tomorrow, the repo must rebuild the whole operation. So commit and push by default, at the end of every session that produced work, and say what you left out.

Media comes first. Zernio keeps an upload in temporary storage for 7 days and copies it to permanent storage only when a post uses it, so Zernio is never the store. Every file a LinkedIn or X post uploads (a card JPG, a carousel PDF, an X image) is committed and pushed before it reaches Zernio. `SCRIPTS/zernio/post.py` and `li_draft.py` refuse an untracked file, and `li_schedule.py` also refuses media that is not on `origin/main`. PNG masters and `src/` folders stay local on purpose, because `card.html` and `meta.json` rebuild them.

Unsafe means a key, a token, a password, a private person's data, or a file over 50 MB. Run a secret scan on the diff before the commit. Never add a co-author line to a commit message.

## Six mistakes a script catches later, not a person

Each one is cheap to avoid now and expensive to find afterwards.

- A file outside the folder structure is invisible to every gate. `coverage.py`,
  the review desk and both scorers glob by folder, so a draft parked elsewhere
  passes every check by never reaching one.
- One file per topic per channel. `coverage.py` counts files, so two channels
  sharing a file report as a gap on the channel that lost.
- Read the source article before you write its social assets. Writing from the
  title alone is where invented metrics come from.
- The banned words live in `SCRIPTS/slop/slop_rules.py`, not in
  `DIGITAL TWIN/Voice.md`, which holds persona. Run
  `python SCRIPTS/slop/score.py "<file>"` rather than checking a list by eye.
- Never invent a fact, a metric or a quote. The runtime contract calls this the
  fabrication rule. It is the one line here where being wrong costs Atharva his
  credibility rather than costing a rewrite.
- Image links use an explicit relative path to `META/Attachments/`, never
  `![[image.png]]`. Obsidian resolves the bare wikilink and every other renderer
  shows a broken image, so the vault looks correct while the published post does
  not.

## Template 2, Pain Then Fix

Rewritten 2026-10-09 from a story post that opened on "A pass meant to cut text on my site added 22 percent more of it." The old version told Atharva's story. The new one hands the reader 3 rules and uses his story as one line of proof.

```
Your website reads heavy, so you spend two days cutting it.

Then you count, and every page is longer than before.

It happened to me. My cut pass added 22 percent more text, because each section I added ran longer than the paragraph it replaced.

Here is the fix in 3 rules:

1. Delete before you add
↳ A new block must replace an old one. Name the block you will remove before you write a word of the new one.

2. Put the prose inside the artifact
↳ If a comparison card already makes the point, turn the paragraphs above it into 3 bullets inside the card. My FAQ page halved this way.

3. Never pin a heading beside a long column
↳ A sticky heading next to a column that runs a screen and a half drifts out of place. Two balanced columns remove the height, and the reason to pin.

"Too long" and "not explained well" are two different complaints. Fix the one you were given.

Which page on your site grew the last time you edited it?
```

What changed, and why each change matters:

1. Line 1 moved from "my site" to "your website", so a stranger sees their own problem.
2. The 22 percent stayed, because it proves the problem is real. It sits in line 3 as one line of proof.
3. Three paragraphs of story became 3 numbered rules with one `↳` line each.
4. The closing aphorism became a question the reader can answer from their own site.

Your AI agent's spend cap is probably a number nobody chose.

FirstRun, my agent that tests docs quickstarts, could spend $0.50 a run. The measured mean was $0.0167, so the cap sat at 30x the real cost.

Sort every number in your agent pricing into 3 buckets:

1. Chosen
Limits you set yourself.
- Free: 1 quickstart a week
- Team: 10 quickstarts a night
- Scale: 100 quickstarts a night, with PRs

2. Under test
Prices you try before you commit.
- Team at $49 a month
- Scale at $299 a month

3. Measured
Numbers only real runs can give you.
- Mean cost per run: $0.0167, from 64 traces
- p95 cost per run: $0.0508
- The spend cap, derived from buckets 2 and 3

Teams get stuck when bucket 3 holds a guess. At the old cap, one bad month costs a $299 customer 5x their fee.

Derive the cap from the price instead.
cap per run = price / runs a month x (1 - margin floor) - compute

@[neatlogs](urn:li:organization:105668039) traced every run and measured the costs. @[cfo.ai](urn:li:organization:106807285) built the plan and set a cap per tier.

"""Render a social card from an HTML file with headless Chromium.

    python render.py <dir>/card.html [--size linkedin|x|x-wide|instagram|square|substack-inline]

The page is laid out at the preset's CSS size and captured at device scale 2,
so a 1080x1350 layout comes out at 2160x2700. Three files land next to the HTML:

  <folder>.png        full resolution master
  <folder>.jpg        quality 92, the file you upload (stays far under 8 MB)
  _preview-540.jpg    the card at phone-feed width. Judge readability on this one.

The folder name is the slug, so cards are always <slug>/card.html.
"""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

SIZES = {
    "linkedin": (1080, 1350),         # 4:5, the tallest single image the LinkedIn feed shows uncropped
    "instagram": (1080, 1350),        # 4:5 feed post
    "x": (1080, 1350),                # 4:5, full height on the X mobile timeline
    "x-wide": (1600, 900),            # 16:9, safe on X desktop and in link previews
    "square": (1080, 1080),
    "substack-inline": (1456, 816),   # in-article image. Hero covers belong to the cover engine
}
SCALE = 2


def render(html: Path, size: str = "linkedin") -> Path:
    w, h = SIZES[size]
    html = html.resolve()
    png = html.with_name(html.parent.name + ".png")
    jpg = html.with_name(html.parent.name + ".jpg")
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        b = p.chromium.launch()
        pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": w, "height": h}, device_scale_factor=SCALE)
        pg.goto(html.as_uri(), wait_until="networkidle")
        pg.evaluate("document.fonts.ready")
        pg.wait_for_timeout(600)
        pg.screenshot(path=str(png), clip={"x": 0, "y": 0, "width": w, "height": h})
        b.close()
    im = Image.open(png).convert("RGB")
    im.save(jpg, quality=92, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    im.resize((540, round(540 * h / w)), Image.LANCZOS).save(html.with_name("_preview-540.jpg"), quality=85)
    return jpg


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("html", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--size", default="linkedin", choices=sorted(SIZES))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    for f in a.html:
        out = render(Path(f), a.size)
        print(out, round(out.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2), "MB")

the dbt DuckDB guide shipped broken. the break is 11 months older than the guide.

the guide says `jafgen --years 6`. FirstRun binary-searched jafgen's releases, one fresh container per probe, and replayed the stored commands:

0.3.1, 2023-01-17: pass
0.4.6, 2024-04-07: fail
no release between them on PyPI
guide merged: 2025-03-14

5 probes, $0 in model calls, because a bisect replays commands and never asks the model.

the finding names the release. the next step fixes the doc. PR #10149 changes the line to `jafgen 6`, and the bisect result sits on that PR as a comment.

when a doc breaks, ask which release broke it before you ask who wrote it. #neatHack

You shipped a fix to your AI agent and it feels better. Measure it before you announce it.

4 mistakes that make an agent fix look better than it is:

1. Testing on new tasks
↳ Run the old version and the new version on the same tasks, in the same clean container. Anything else measures the tasks.

2. Reading only the pass rate
↳ My agent went from 2 of 4 quickstarts finished to 3 of 4. Its time per run also grew from 128 to 201 seconds.

3. Counting cost from two sources
↳ On 43 runs, my agent's own cost counter read 39% higher than the tracing tool. Pick one source and name it.

4. Calling a slower run a regression
↳ The new version fixes a failed step and reruns it, so it takes longer. It recovered 3 failed steps, and the old one recovered 0.

I ran this on FirstRun, my agent that tests docs quickstarts, during the #neatHack hackathon. @[neatlogs](urn:li:organization:105668039) traced all 8 runs, and cost per run fell from $0.0262 to $0.0200.

---
type: LinkedIn Post
title: Four Quickstart Breaks a New Developer Hits First
source_blog: none
description: "Your quickstart broke since launch, and the first person to find out is a new user. Four real breaks from one weekend."
created: 2026-10-11
updated: 2026-10-11
posted: false
---

Your quickstart broke since launch, and the first person to find out is a new user.

I spent the #neatHack weekend on an agent that runs a quickstart the way a new developer would, in a clean container. It found 4 breaks in 48 hours:

1. A removed flag
↳ The dbt DuckDB guide says jafgen --years 6. jafgen dropped that flag in version 0.4.6, 11 months before the guide shipped.

2. A missing Python version
↳ The same guide's repo pins networkx 3.7, which needs Python 3.12. The guide names no version.

3. A PATH gap after install
↳ The Entire CLI installs cleanly, then a fresh shell says command not found, because ~/.local/bin is missing from PATH.

4. A stale version number
↳ An AccuKnox page names knoxctl 0.9.0. The installer pulls 0.9.58.

Each break is now an open PR with a replay of the failing step and a clean rerun.

The agent is FirstRun. @[neatlogs](urn:li:organization:105668039) traced every run, @[Entire](urn:li:organization:111845019) recorded every coding session, and @[cfo.ai](urn:li:organization:106807285) built the business plan. The video shows one run end to end.

Run your own quickstart in a fresh container before your next release.

Which step in your quickstart has nobody run since launch?
